The Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal,
vide order dated 27.04.2015, treated the DAR, as claim petition U/s 166(4) of the M.V. Act.

It was further averred that at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was driven in a rash and negligent manner, by its driver Pardeep Kumar Manocha S/o Sh.

vide order dated 27.04.2015, treated the DAR, as claim petition U/s 166(4) of the M.V. Act.

R1 and R2 have not contested the DAR/claim petition, by filing any written statement and later,
they were proceeded Ex-parte, vide order 21.05.2018.

Thus, this Tribunal deems it appropriate, to award compensation of Rs.9,001/-, to the petitioner, under the head of medical expenses.
The petitioner has claimed compensation, on account of special diet and conveyance, as a result of the injuries sustained by Vinod Kumar (since deceased), prior to his death.
The legal heirs of the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased) has claimed compensation, on account of attendant charges, as a result of the injuries, sustained in the case accident.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even otherwise, since R1 failed to file any written statement and also failed to cross- examine PW2, despite being granted opportunity, therefore, he deemed to have admitted, that there was rashness and negligence, on the part of R1, in causing the accident in question.
Further, R1 also failed to prove, that he has ever approached to any higher authority,
with respect to his false implication, in the present case.
Consequently, in MACT No. 450682/16 Page 19 of36 Vinod Kumar vs Pardeep Kumar and Ors. Page 20 of36 view of the unrebutted testimony of PW1, it stands duly proved, that the accident had taken place, due to rash and negligent driving, of the offending vehicle by R1.
It has to be borne in mind, that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.

Accordingly, the entitlement of the petitioner, to compensation if any, towards special diet and conveyance charges,
has to be determined, in accordance with the nature of injuries, sustained by the victim Vinod Kumar, in the case accident.
In the present matter, it is worthwhile to mention here, that when DAR was filed, the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased) was alive hence, DAR was filed, in order to seek compensation, qua the accidental injuries, sustained by the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased) but, during the course of trial, victim Vinod Kumar expired on 20.02.2017 and thereafter, his legal heirs lead their evidence, so as to prove, that the death of the deceased, was due to accidental injuries and accordingly, it was argued that compensation be awarded accordingly.

However, perusal of the medical record of the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased), reveals that after the accident, on examination of the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased), the doctor has given the opinion, that he has sustained grievous injuries and he remains admitted at Deen Dayal Hospital, from 22.06.2014 to 25.06.2014 (3 days) and from 31.07.2014 to 03.09.2014 (34 days).

Therefore, keeping in view the grievous nature of injuries, sustained by the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased) and after taking into consideration, his last medical bill dated 09.04.2015, the treatment cum recuperation period, in case of the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased), is determined to be about 10 months and during this period, the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased)
must have incurred expenses on special diet, required for his speedy recovery, as well as on travel to various hospitals and clinics, from his residence and vice versa.
They have however, not disclosed the exact expenditure, incurred by the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased),
on availing services of a medical attendant, during his treatment period.
However, as discussed above, regarding the medical condition of the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased), as per which, Vinod Kumar has sustained grievous injuries in the case accident, and remains hospitalized for a period of 37 days, in Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital and determination of his period of treatment cum recuperation as 10 months, this Tribunal is of the opinion, that due to the injuries sustained by the victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased), in the case accident, he must have required services of either a paid attendant or a family member, as an attendant for his self-care activities.
Thus, this Tribunal deems it appropriate, to award a lump sum amount of Rs.20,000/-, as compensation to the petitioner, under this head towards attendant charges.
While deciding the compensation under the head of pain and suffering, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in a case titled as "Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon &
Ors., has disallowed the compensation under the head pain and suffering, being personal injuries.
Thus, as the victim Vinod Kumar (since MACT No. 450682/16 Page 26 of36 Vinod Kumar vs Pardeep Kumar and Ors. Page 27 of36 deceased) expired, during the pendency of the proceedings,
therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
PW1 has though placed on record photocopy of admission ticket of victim Vinod Kumar (since deceased),
for appearing in exam of 3rd year of graduation course and photocopy of his 2 nd year marksheet but, PW1 failed to prove the same, by producing original thereof therefore, the said documents cannot be taken into consideration.
But, as R3 also failed to elicit any admission from the testimony of PW1, so as to prove that the victim Vinod Kumar was not doing any work, therefore, Vinod Kumar is taken as self employed person and thus, entitled to minimum wages, payable to an unskilled person.
